text:
Carolina arrives in St. Louis stinging from a 6-5 shootout loss at Edmonton, where the Oilers erased a two-goal deficit. The Hurricanes are 3-1-1 in their last five, and they've held the edge in expected goals (the quality of chances) in all five games, so the results have trailed the play. They're missing Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal. Bradly Nadeau has stepped in beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake, and Mark Jankowski has taken Staal's spot but is now day-to-day. St. Louis is 3-2-0 in its last five and comes off a 6-2 win over Vegas, where Aleksanteri Kaskimaki picked up his first NHL point.

Carolina's 58% share of expected goals at five on five tops St. Louis's 51%, and it has the stronger power play (0.96 expected goals a game to 0.54). The catch is discipline: the Hurricanes take 4.25 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Pyotr Kochetkov (+2.5 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what the shots should yield) and Joel Hofer (+3.6) are both ahead of expectation. Hofer has the track record, at +11.1 last season over 46 games against Kochetkov's -0.03 over nine. Our model has CAR at 3.26 expected goals tonight and STL at 2.67.

Watch Sebastian Aho, with a 34% chance to score and a 72% chance at a point, and Jackson Blake, one point from 100 career points. Jankowski has goals in six straight games, though the numbers say he's due to cool. For St. Louis, Dylan Holloway carries a six-game point streak.
